Reverse-engineered the actual IL instead (dnfile+dncil via a throwaway venv, ReGrowthCore.dll 1.6): ProcessMap flood-fills Mineable things with building.isNaturalRock==true into a lumps dict (skipping any defName in ModSettings_PerspectiveOres.skippedMineableDefs), AssociateLumps assigns each lump a Color borrowed from an adjacent isNaturalRock&&!isResourceRock neighbour's DrawColor, then queues RecolorMineables (b__0) and a 2nd independent long-event action (b__1) separately -- so b__0 crashing does NOT stop b__1 or the rest of map load; blast radius is cosmetic-only (some mineables miss their recolor tint) and self-contained, matching the log (1x/load, no crash, no cascade). RecolorMineables throws when accessing thing.Graphic.data (a GraphicData) -- null there is the only NRE-shaped read in the method. Cross-checked EVERY isNaturalRock ThingDef in the current def dump (defs.sqlite, mods=623, captured 2026-09-24) against this exact criterion: 174 total across all mods, 52 of ours (RM_/RSW_/RUT_/mandrake.* -- KOTOR_/RUT_ rock+ore veins, GravTide_ variants) -- ALL 52 have graphicData present with populated texPath/graphicClass and a cachedGraphic whose .data is a valid self-reference (no null, no missing field). Zero anomalies found in ours or in any of the other 571 mods' defs. Caveat: the dump is a post-load snapshot, so a graphic that failed once during FinalizeInit but got rebuilt cleanly afterward by the normal render path would look healthy here too -- a static dump cannot rule that out. What would resolve it: a live Harmony postfix/breakpoint on RecolorMineables (or the exception handler) on the Desktop machine, logging the actual Thing/def whose Graphic.data was null at the moment of the throw -- needs a live debugger or an injected diagnostic DLL, not obtainable from Player.log or the def dump. No fixable defect found on our side; not closing/guessing.

Autonomous-tick progress (shas 8e4efd343, 6d55fbbe4, 0c264fd5c): four more
REDs diagnosed and fixed via static analysis only (no bridge/quicktest --
none was loaded this session):
1. ROOT CAUSE behind Antiquities' wait_ticks(95000) FAIL and ShipMemory's
   wait_ticks(700) FAIL: modcheck.suite.TestContext.wait_ticks made one
   un-verified rimworld/step_game_ticks call and trusted its own report --
   that tool silently truncates well below the ticks requested under load
   (measured 600-2800/call, silent-failures.md). Fixed at the shared
   helper: now loops in chunks verified against the real ticksGame, raises
   if the clock genuinely stalls. This likely also explains other still-
   unread REDs in the list below that use large wait_ticks values --
   worth re-checking before assuming they need their own fix.
2. ROOT CAUSE behind RimProperty's chain-setup abort AND (newly found)
   half of Aftermath's 0/3: both assumed a Pirate FactionDef with
   requiredCountAtGameStart>0 guarantees a live Faction instance. False
   here, always: Biotech's PirateWaster pre-empts vanilla Pirate at
   worldgen (jawa/faction_create's own docstring), and every test list
   mandates all five expansions. Added TestContext.ensure_faction(),
   wired into both suites via jawa/faction_create.
3. Aftermath's other 0/3 component: harmony_patches_registered called
   jawa/harmony_patches(harmonyId=...) -- no such parameter (declared:
   typeName, methodName). Rewritten to query per patched (type, method)
   seam (read off each Patch_*.cs's own [HarmonyPatch] attribute) and
   check owner on the real result shape. Aftermath should now be 3/3
   pending live re-verify.
4. ResearchRetag 1/2: core_rows_match_manifest compared str(700.0) against
   "700" for baseCost -- a numeric field, not a string one -- and always
   mismatched even when the patch applied exactly as authored. Fixed with
   a numeric fallback compare.
5. StructureInjections 1/2 (different mod from StructureInjectionsRUT):
   moisture_farm_plan_replays' floor already accounted for a 6-item
   Armoury shortfall but still measured 1 short (92 vs floor 93). Traced
   to a GENUINE mod-content defect, not a suite bug: the plan's one
   PrimitiveWell THING line names a defName that does not exist ANYWHERE
   in any mod or DLC (checked against the live Mods folder + Data/ tree
   directly) -- traced to design/Jawa/templates/{cistern,moisture_farm,
   oasis_shrine,trading_post}.lua, all four of which reference the same
   dead name, shipping into 8 installed .txt plans across 4 mods. Left
   RED on purpose (raising the floor would launder a real bug into
   GREEN) and filed PRIMITIVEWELL_DEAD_DEFNAME_1 to track the actual fix
   (correct the templates or author the def for real).

title: RUT_TarVault ships with tickerType unset (defaults Never) -- CompTick never fires, whole tar-vault seal mechanism is dead code

text: Found in the DIRTY_CODE_REVIEW_STANDING_LOOP_1 TheSump wave: src/RimUtinni/UtinniPatches/Defs/ThingDefs_Buildings/RUT_TarVault.xml (ParentName=StorageShelfBase) never sets tickerType, and neither does StorageShelfBase/ShelfBase/FurnitureBase/BuildingBase anywhere in the chain (checked live via RimSage get_def_details on vanilla Shelf's own merged def -- confirmed no tickerType field anywhere). ThingDef.tickerType has no field initializer so it defaults to TickerType.Never (enum 0), and TickManager.TickListFor returns null for Never (Source/Verse/TickManager.cs:310) -- the Thing is on no tick list at all, so Tick()/CompTick() never fires. RM_Comp_TarVaultSeal.CompTick() (src/RimMandrake/TheSump/Source/RM_Comp_TarVaultSeal.cs) is therefore dead code on the only ThingDef that carries it: the vault never seals anything, the whole SUMP_TAR_VAULT_1 mechanism (rot-freeze, forbid, solvent-gated extraction) is currently inert in a real game. Fix: add <tickerType>Normal</tickerType> to RUT_TarVault.xml. A defensive ConfigErrors check was added to CompProperties_TarVaultSeal.ConfigErrors (same wave, TheSump commit) so any def wiring this comp without tickerType Normal now surfaces a dev-mode config error naming the fix -- same pattern vanilla itself uses for this exact trap (CompProperties_SelfhealHitpoints.cs / CompProperties_FacilityInUse.cs).

text: 2026-09-27 FOUNDRY (source-only, no live repro): read Find.World/WorldInterface/TilePicker, TickManager.ForcePaused and LongEventHandler.ExecuteToExecuteWhenFinished from decompiled 1.6 source via RimSage. Confirmed root cause: Find.World (Find.cs ~100-108) is genuinely null throughout this session -- Current.Game.World never got assigned, i.e. world/map generation itself stalled or silently failed at 623 mods and never completed. Find.WorldInterface/TilePicker NRE through that null (Find.cs ~212/220); TickManager.ForcePaused (TickManager.cs ~142) reads Find.TilePicker.Active first, so anything evaluating it while World is null NREs the same way. LongEventHandler does not itself retry a failed post-action -- it logs once and clears -- so the REPEATING log lines mean something (a UI-sync callback or RimBridge's own readiness poll) kept re-queuing fresh post-actions against a world that never finished existing, not one action looping. The second exception (get_MapUI InvalidCastException) is an ordinary, expected consequence of the same fact -- MapUI only exists once ProgramState reaches Playing, which it never did -- not a separate engine bug. Nothing here is fixable by editing our own C#: the stall is upstream of any bridge tool call, inside vanilla world-gen itself. Genuinely needs a live repro with mod-list bisection (does it reproduce at a smaller count than 623? at 599?) to find the actual hung GenStep/WorldGenStep or colliding Harmony patch -- not attempted this pass. text: 2026-09-27 FOUNDRY, MAJOR CORRECTION: the earlier source-only note here (same day) recommended a mod-list bisection on the theory this needs 'high mod count' -- that theory is WRONG, disproven live. rimworld/start_debug_game_ready reproduces the IDENTICAL crash on a 9-MOD bare-bones list (brrainz.harmony + Core + all 5 DLC + brrainz.rimbridgeserver + one content mod, mandrake.rm.miasma) -- confirmed 3x across 2 fresh relaunches, once with VEF+AlienWorlds+TidallyLocked present (which added their own transpiler/prefix frames to the trace but were NOT the cause) and once without them at all (identical stack, no VEF/AlienWorlds frames). Real root cause, read straight from Player.log: System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException inside RimWorld.Planet.WorldGrid.get_Item(PlanetTile) <- WorldPathGrid.CalculatedMovementDifficultyAt <- RecalculatePerceivedMovementDifficultyAt <- RecalculateLayerPerceivedPathCosts <- RecalculateAllLayersPathCosts <- World.FinalizeInit <- WorldGenerator.GenerateWorld <- Verse.Root_Play.SetupForQuickTestPlay <- RimBridgeServer.LifecycleCapabilityModule.StartDebugGameCore. This throws for EVERY WorldFeatureDef during world-feature generation too ('Could not generate world features of def Island/Archipelago/.../Grasslands', same exception, dozens of lines) and once more as an uncaught async exception afterward. Fits the earlier fork's finding exactly: Current.Game.World never gets assigned because WORLD GENERATION ITSELF throws mid-FinalizeInit, so nothing downstream (bridge token issued at OS/engine level, but Find.World null) ever recovers. Best-guess mechanism (unverified further): Odyssey's multi-PlanetLayer world (surface + orbit) plus SetupForQuickTestPlay's small/fast quicktest-scale world generation undersizes or mis-sizes one PlanetLayer's WorldGrid tile array while RecalculateAllLayersPathCosts iterates ALL layers assuming a consistent size -- a full-size real-game worldgen (the owner's actual play path) may not hit this at all, since it was never observed failing on the real canonical save/world. NOT reproducible-fixed by us: this is vanilla Root_Play.SetupForQuickTestPlay, not our code, not RimBridge's own code (RimBridge just invokes the vanilla debug entry point). This means rimworld/start_debug_game_ready is CURRENTLY UNUSABLE for any FOUNDRY live-proof workflow, full stop, regardless of mod list -- every skill/prove_*.py script that opens with it needs a different path (rimworld/load_game_ready against an existing compatible save, if one exists, is the only alternative found so far; none exists for the minimal or bare-bones lists as of this note). Did not attempt a vanilla-side fix (Harmony workaround) this pass -- out of scope for the item that surfaced it (MIASMA_SCUTTLER_PREDATION_1).
